title: What the Net Cannot See
logline: Night after night, a small lagoon-fishing crew works by lamplight where most of what reaches them never becomes a catch, a flicker at the edge of sight, a sound not quite placed, and only a few signals ever become a decision to strike.

object.note: Object 5 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: The salt pans' daylight turns to a lagoon at night, where most of what reaches the crew, a flicker, a splash, never becomes a decision.

thread_out.thread: From signals at the edge of sight in the dark to the half-light of a pre-dawn flower market, where colour is seen before any flower is named.

requirements: A working lagoon, estuary or shallow reef fished at night
A crew willing to be filmed through long, low-light hours
Safe water access for a small camera crew at night

lesson.in_simple_terms: Most of what touches our senses never becomes an experience at all: it arrives too faintly or too late and simply fades. Only the strongest signals get the mind's full run and a response.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අපේ ඉන්ද්‍රියයන්ට ගැටෙන බොහෝ දේ කිසිදු දැනීමක් නොවී මැකී යන අතර, ප්‍රතිචාරයක් දක්වා යන්නේ ප්‍රබලව එන දේවල් කිහිපයක් පමණි.
lesson.the_teaching: Margaya grades what meets the senses as very great, great, slight or very slight, by how prominent it is (size, light, nearness) and by how late in its short life it strikes the sense (C040). The stronger the object, the more of the process runs; a very slight object only makes the resting mind waver, and the texts call these 'empty rounds' (mogha-vāra), with no knowing of the object at all (C040, C045). A slight object is sorted but never reaches impulsion, so it is only feebly known and, on the source's account, produces no action (C045). Beneath all of this is the bare, rootless layer of seeing and hearing, which the texts say needs a working sense, an object, a medium such as light, and attention (C009).
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Long stretches of dark water and a watched float, with nothing visibly changing, are the film's main texture. Against them, a turned head at a splash, and a decision to cast or to let it pass, stand out sharply. The quiet talk between casts about what someone thought they saw lets the viewer feel how little of the night ever registered.

key_terms.en: 'empty' or futile round: a process with no cognitive moments

lesson.caution: This is not a claim that faint signals secretly shape us, nor a promise that careful attention can catch everything: the texts tie how vivid something is to conditions such as light, distance and the state of the senses.
lesson.builds_on: The salt pans showed things renewing too fast to notice; this film asks which of the things passing the senses the mind actually takes up, and the answer is very few.
lesson.evidence_class: editorial interpretation grounded in cited source teaching
